topic.name: The Axis of Symmetry of a Parabola

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=kx^2+3x-15$ is $x=4.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, we will set our result equal to $4.$

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=k$ and $b=3$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get

\begin{align*} x &= -\dfrac{3}{2(k)}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3}{2k}. \end{align*}

We already know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4,$ so we must have

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{3}{2k} &= 4 \\[5pt] -3 &= 8k \\[5pt] k &= -\dfrac{3}{8}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding an Unknown Coefficient Given the Axis of Symmetry

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=2x^2+12x+6.$
question.explanation:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=2$ and $b=12$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x&=-\dfrac{12}{2(2)}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{12}{4}\\[5pt] &=-3. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=-3.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=-3$ into the original equation: \begin{align*} y &= 2x^2+12x+6 \\[5pt] &= 2(-3)^2+12(-3)+6 \\[5pt] &= 18-36+6 \\[5pt] &= -12 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $(-3,-12).$

example.title: Finding the Vertex of a Parabola

question.text: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $y=4x^2-2x+1.$
question.explanation:
The vertex of the parabola lies on the axis of symmetry, so we will start by computing the axis of symmetry.

The equation of the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is given by

\[ x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}. \]

Substituting $a=4$ and $b=-2$ into the formula for the axis of symmetry, we get \begin{align*} x&=-\dfrac{-2}{2(4)}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{-2}{8}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the equation of the axis of symmetry is $x=\dfrac{1}{4}.$ This also represents the $x$-coordinate of the vertex. To find the $y$-coordinate of the vertex, we substitute $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$ into the original equation:

\begin{align*} y &= 4x^2-2x+1 \\[5pt] &= 4\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^2-2\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)+1 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}+1 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{2}{4}+\dfrac{4}{4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{4} \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is at $\left(\dfrac{1}{4},\dfrac{3}{4}\right).$
